title: CT Abdomen Pelvis with Contrast
premedication: Oral contrast: 900 mL Readi-Cat 2 over 90 minutes. Last cup 30 min before scan

notes.tech: Ensure adequate oral contrast opacification. Scan from diaphragm through pubic symphysis. 70 second delay typical
notes.nursing: 20-22G IV required. Verify patent IV. Oral contrast 250-500mL water before scan.
notes.rad: Systematic review of all solid organs. Check for free fluid/air. Assess bowel enhancement pattern
notes.tips: Arms raised completely. Remove all metal objects from scan range
notes.additional_recons: Thin slice 1mm for 3D if mass identified

safety.allergy: Check allergy history. Pre-medicate if prior reaction

notes.tech: THREE phases: 1) Non-contrast for absolute HU 2) Portal venous 70s 3) 15 MINUTE delayed for washout. All phases cover adrenals
notes.nursing: 20-22G IV. Patient must wait 15 min for delayed phase
notes.rad: NC: lipid-rich adenoma < 10 HU. Portal venous: enhancement. 15 min delay: calculate washout (adenoma shows washout)
notes.tips: Patient wait time 15 min. Measure HU carefully with ROI in same location
notes.additional_recons: Calculate absolute washout: (Enhanced HU - Delayed HU)/(Enhanced HU - NC HU) x 100. >60% suggests adenoma. Measure HU in all phases

safety.allergy: Check allergy history. Explain 15 min delay

title: CT Biphasic Pancreas
author: Dr. Williams
premedication: Water PO: 900 mL water orally 15-30 min before scan for gastric/duodenal distension

contrast.timing: Dual phase: Pancreatic arterial + Portal venous

notes.tech: TWO phases: Pancreatic phase (40-45s or bolus track) + Portal venous (70s). Water for negative contrast
notes.nursing: 18-20G IV. Ensure water intake for duodenal distension
notes.rad: Pancreatic phase: optimal pancreatic enhancement and small lesions. Portal venous: liver and venous structures
notes.tips: Water distension of duodenum helpful. Thin slices for pancreas
notes.additional_recons: Curved MPR pancreatic duct. MIP pancreatic vasculature

safety.allergy: Check allergy history. Coordinate water intake

title: CT Chest Abdomen Pelvis with Contrast
author: Dr. Smith
npo: NPO 4 hours solids. Clear liquids OK up to 2 hours
premedication: Oral contrast: 250-500 mL neutral (Volumen or water). Give 60-90 min before scan

notes.tech: Single phase portal venous. 40 second injection. 70 second scan delay from start of injection
notes.nursing: 20-22G IV. Verify renal function
notes.rad: Portal venous phase optimal for solid organ and bowel assessment. Systematic review all organs
notes.tips: Arms fully raised. Neutral oral contrast preferred over positive
notes.additional_recons: Sagittal reformats optional

title: CT Cystogram
author: Dr. Kim
premedication: Bladder contrast: 350-400 mL dilute contrast (30 mL contrast in 350 mL saline)

notes.tech: TWO components: 1) Non-contrast CT 2) Bladder filling via Foley with dilute contrast 3) Scan distended bladder. Coordinate with nursing
notes.nursing: Foley catheter required. Dilute contrast preparation (30mL in 350mL saline). Gravity fill bladder. Patient signals fullness
notes.rad: Cystogram: bladder integrity extravasation
notes.tips: Adequate bladder distension critical. Gravity fill slowly. Clamp Foley during scan
notes.additional_recons: Compare distended vs non-contrast. Document extravasation location. 3D reformation if complex injury

safety.renal: eGFR doesn't matter, contrast not excreted

title: CT Enterography
author: Dr. Martinez
premedication: Neutral oral contrast (VoLumen): 1st bottle (450mL) at 90 min. 2nd bottle (450mL) at 60 min. Half bottle (225mL) at 30 min. Other half (225mL) at 5 min before scan

notes.tech: Enterographic phase (45 sec). High volume neutral oral for bowel distension. 25 second injection. Scan 45 sec from start
notes.nursing: 18-20G IV. Ensure adequate oral contrast intake (total ~1350mL). May need anti-peristaltic agent
notes.rad: Assess bowel wall enhancement and thickness. Look for strictures fistulas abscesses. Mesenteric vascularity
notes.tips: Adequate oral contrast distension critical. High injection rate
notes.additional_recons: Curved MPR of bowel segments. Mesenteric vascular assessment

safety.allergy: Check allergy history. Coordinate oral contrast timing

contrast.volume: Split bolus: 1st injection 1.1 mL/kg + 2nd injection 0.4 mL/kg

notes.tech: COMPLEX protocol: 1) NC (optional stone protocol) 2) 1st contrast injection 3) Early PV 60s after 1st 4) WAIT 5-7 min 5) 2nd injection + saline 6) Excretory/IVP 90-120s after 2nd
notes.nursing: 18-20G IV. Split bolus technique. May give Lasix 10-20mg IV for better opacification
notes.rad: NC optional: detect stones. Early PV: renal parenchyma. Excretory: collecting system ureters bladder for urothelial lesions
notes.tips: Split bolus critical for opacification. Lasix may help. Prone imaging optional for ureters
notes.additional_recons: MIP urogram coronal and sagittal. Curved MPR of ureters. 3D urogram

notes.tech: LOW DOSE protocol. Reduced mAs. Cover kidneys to pubic symphysis. Stone protocol settings
notes.nursing: No IV needed. No oral contrast. Explain low radiation technique
notes.rad: Look for stones - measure size and location. Check for hydronephrosis. Assess for alternative diagnoses
notes.tips: Low dose protocol. Reduced mAs. Image quality adequate for stones
notes.additional_recons: Thin slice 1mm for small stones. Stone size measurements

contrast.volume: Split bolus: 1st injection 1.1 mL/kg + 2nd injection 0.4 mL/kg

notes.tech: COMPLEX protocol: 1) NC 2) 1st contrast injection 3) Arterial 20s after 1st 4) WAIT 5-7 min 5) 2nd injection + saline 6) IVP/nephrographic 90-120s after 2nd
notes.nursing: 18-20G IV. Explain split bolus technique and delay
notes.rad: NC: fat/calcification. Arterial: vascular anatomy and hypervascular masses. Nephrographic/IVP: delayed enhancement and collecting system
notes.tips: Split bolus timing critical. 5-7 min wait between injections
notes.additional_recons: Compare NC vs arterial vs nephrographic. Measure HU in mass. MIP urogram

contrast.timing: Triple phase: NC + Arterial + Portal Venous + Delayed

notes.tech: FOUR acquisitions: 1) NC abdomen 2) Late arterial (bolus track or 30-35s) 3) Portal venous 70s 4) Delayed 5 min. FOV: Abdomen for NC/Art/Delay. Full AP for PV | Injection duration is fixed at 25 s
notes.nursing: 20-22G IV. High flow rate critical
notes.rad: NC: characterize lesion. Arterial: hypervascular lesions HCC. Portal: most liver lesions. Delayed: washout pattern
notes.tips: High flow rate. Extended 5 min delay. Breath hold coaching

title: Calcium Score
premedication: HR control not needed for calcium score

notes.tech: Prospective ECG gating. | Suspended Respiration breathing instructions. | For single source CT: Target End Diastole if HR < 63BPM, else target End diastole and end systole. For dual source CT: Target End diastole if HR <79, else target end systole. Ensure ECG leads well connected, Goal: <= 60 BPM, regular (+/- 5).
notes.nursing: No IV needed.
notes.rad: Check breathing motion on lung FOV. Calculate Agatston score. Report percentile for age/sex. Document coronary calcification distribution
notes.tips: Good ECG tracing essential. Patient breath hold coaching
notes.additional_recons: Agatston score calculation. Percentile reporting

title: Coronary CTA
premedication: HR < 60 target. | Metoprolol 5mg IV increments up to 15mg. Metoprolol contraindications include sBP < 100, 2nd/3rd degree heart block, and inhaler dependent asthma. | Nitroglycerin 0.4mg SL 5 minutes before scan. Nitroglycerin contraindications include sBP < 100, PDE5 inhibitors within 48 hrs, severe aortic stenosis.

notes.additional_recons: Curved MPR of all coronaries.
notes.nursing: 20G IV minimum. Check for metoprolol or nitroglycerin contraindications. Nitro is priority over metoprolol if BP is borderline.
notes.rad: Calculate Agatston score. Give CAD-RADS score. Check function look for potential focal wall motion abnormalities
notes.tech: Non-valsalva breathing technique, cardiac breathing instruction. Put in study notes if patient unable to follow breathing instructions. | If high HR variability, can trigger by millisecond (200ms - 450 ms pulse range). Revolution CT is better for Afib. | Target End diastole if HR < 65bpm. Target End systole if HR > 86bpm. Target End diastole to End systole if HR 66 - 75 bpm
notes.tips: Full chest coverage essential. Extended FOV. Low pitch for retrospective gating

title: Coronary CTA Post-CABG
premedication: HR < 60 target. | Metoprolol 5mg IV increments up to 15mg. Metoprolol contraindications include sBP < 100, 2nd/3rd degree heart block, and inhaler dependent asthma. | Nitroglycerin 0.4mg SL 5 minutes before scan. Nitroglycerin contraindications include sBP < 100, PDE5 inhibitors within 48 hrs, severe aortic stenosis.

recons.notes: Thin slice for grafts and native vessels

notes.tech: Non-valsalva breathing technique, cardiac breathing instruction. Put in study notes if patient unable to follow breathing instructions. | If high HR variability, can trigger by millisecond (200ms - 450 ms pulse range). Revolution CT is better for Afib. | Target End diastole if HR < 65bpm. Target End systole if HR > 86bpm. Target End diastole to End systole if HR 66 - 75 bpm
notes.nursing: 20G IV minimum. Check for metoprolol or nitroglycerin contraindications. Nitro is priority over metoprolol if BP is borderline.
notes.rad: Assess all grafts: LIMA RIMA SVG. Check anastomoses. Native vessel disease. Graft patency vs occlusion. Check functional series for WMA.
notes.tips: Full chest coverage essential. Extended FOV. Low pitch for retrospective gating
notes.additional_recons: Curved MPR of all grafts. Label LIMA RIMA SVG.

title: Endocarditis/Cardiac Mass
premedication: HR < 65 preferred. No premedication typically given.

series.name: Delayed phase
series.notes: To detect for abscess, vegetation, masses

notes.tech: Non-valsalva breathing technique, cardiac breathing instruction. | Injection duration is fixed 35 sec fixed 30 sec scan delay. Retrospective gating trigger at 30-70% (End sys - end dia).  Reconstruct  at 5% intervals.
notes.nursing: 18-20G IV. HR control helpful but not critical
notes.rad: Assess all valves for vegetations. Evaluate myocardium for abscess. Look for intracardiac masses. Check for complications
notes.tips: Multiple cardiac phases helpful for valve motion. Thin slices for vegetations
notes.additional_recons: Multi-phase reconstructions. 4-chamber 2-chamber views. Valve-specific reformats

notes.tech: TWO acquisitions: 1) Gated retrospective CHEST 2) Flash helical ABDOMEN/PELVIS. Chest gated for aortic root. AP flash arterial
notes.nursing: 20G IV minimum
notes.rad: Gated chest: assess aortic root valve coronaries. Flash AP: assess aorta and branches. Combined cardiac and vascular
notes.tips: Arms up. Careful timing between gated and flash acquisitions
notes.additional_recons: Curved MPR full aorta. Aortic valve reformats. 3D VR

notes.tech: THREE acquisitions: 1) Gated CHEST 2) Flash AP arterial 3) CHEST venogram 60 sec delay. Venous for retrosternal structures
notes.nursing: 20G IV
notes.rad: Gated: cardiac anatomy. Arterial: systemic vessels. VENOUS: retrosternal veins and adherent structures critical for surgical planning
notes.tips: Venous phase critical for surgical planning. Map all retrosternal structures
notes.additional_recons: 3D VR venogram highlighting retrosternal veins. Distance measurements sternum to heart

safety.allergy: Large contrast load - verify renal function

notes.tips: High kV (130-140) critical for metal artifact. Increased contrast volume
notes.additional_recons: Multi-phase reconstructions. Valve-specific views. Paravalvular assessment

notes.tech: Orbits: superior orbital rim to maxillary sinus. Axial 1-2mm. Coronal reformats. NC for trauma. Contrast for masses/inflammation
notes.nursing: Contrast for mass or inflammation. NC for trauma and metallic foreign body
notes.rad: Extraocular muscles. Optic nerve. Globe integrity. Orbital fat. Preseptal vs postseptal. Masses. Foreign body
notes.tips: Angle axial parallel to optic nerves. Thin slices
notes.additional_recons: Assess optic nerve canal. Measure EOMs if thyroid eye disease. Document foreign body

notes.tech: FOUR phases: 1) NC 2) Arterial 25s 3) Venous 55s 4) Delayed/washout 90s. Skull base to mediastinum. Parathyroid enhances early washes out
notes.nursing: 18-20G IV. High flow rate for arterial
notes.rad: NC: baseline. Arterial: parathyroid lights up. Venous: thyroid enhances. Delayed: parathyroid washes out faster than thyroid
notes.tips: Four phase critical. Look for early enhancement and washout
notes.additional_recons: Subtraction images. Compare all phases. Document location for surgeon. Measure size

notes.tech: Coronal acquisition skull base through maxillary sinuses. Submillimeter for anatomy. Bone and soft tissue windows
notes.nursing: No IV. Remove dentures and metal
notes.rad: Assess all sinuses. Ostiomeatal complex. Anatomic variants. Mucosal thickening. Polyps. Bony anatomy
notes.tips: Direct coronal preferred. Submillimeter for anatomy
notes.additional_recons: Document anatomic variants (Haller cells concha bullosa). OMC assessment

notes.tech: Submillimeter isotropic acquisition. DICOM for surgical navigation system. May need fiducial markers. Entire sinus anatomy
notes.nursing: Position as for surgery. Fiducials if required
notes.rad: Complete sinus anatomy for surgical navigation. Ostiomeatal complex. Skull base. Lamina papyracea
notes.tips: Isotropic voxels essential. DICOM for navigation
notes.additional_recons: Export DICOM to surgical navigation system. Isotropic 0.625mm

notes.tech: Skull base to thoracic inlet. 60-70 sec delay for venous phase. Arms down. Minimize swallowing. May need NC if calcium assessment
notes.nursing: 18-20G IV. Coach no swallowing during scan
notes.rad: Assess neck spaces. Retropharyngeal. Parapharyngeal. Masticator. Parotid. Submandibular. Thyroid. Lymph nodes. Abscess vs phlegmon
notes.tips: Arms down. Minimize swallowing. Quiet breathing
notes.additional_recons: Assess all neck spaces. Measure lymph nodes. Airway diameter if concern

notes.tech: Temporal bones: external auditory canal to petrous apex. SUBMILLIMETER <0.625mm. Direct axial and direct coronal if possible. Ultra high resolution
notes.nursing: No IV. Remove hearing aids and earrings
notes.rad: Ossicles. Cochlea. Semicircular canals. Internal auditory canal. Mastoid air cells. Cholesteatoma. Fracture. Tegmen
notes.tips: Submillimeter critical. Sharp bone kernel. Remove all metal
notes.additional_recons: Pöschl and Stenvers oblique reformats for IAC. Measure vestibular aqueduct

notes.tech: C7 to L1. Submillimeter helical. Sagittal and coronal reformats. Arms up if possible
notes.nursing: No IV unless contrast indicated. Arms up to reduce artifact
notes.rad: Alignment. Compression fractures. Pedicles. Spinal canal. Disc spaces. Paraspinal soft tissues
notes.tips: Arms up reduces artifact. Bone algorithm

notes.tech: NC Head optional then CTA skull base to vertex. Bolus tracking. Submillimeter for 3D reconstruction
notes.nursing: 20G IV minimum. Good bolus essential
notes.rad: Assess circle of Willis. Aneurysms. Stenosis. Vascular malformations. Anatomic variants
notes.tips: Minimize motion. Thin slices for small aneurysms
notes.additional_recons: 3D VR and MIP. Measure aneurysm if present. Assess A1 A2 dominance

title: CTA Head and Neck (Arch to Vertex)
position: Supine head-first with arms at sides
premedication: None typically. Consider anxiolytic if severe claustrophobia

series.name: CTA Head
series.notes: Same bolus as neck - single acquisition

notes.tech: Scan from aortic arch through vertex. Use bolus tracking in arch. Minimize dental artifact with gantry angulation
notes.nursing: Good antecubital IV access required - 20G minimum. Verify injection site for extravasation risk
notes.rad: Evaluate complete circle of Willis. Assess carotid bifurcations. Look for dissection. Check aneurysms
notes.tips: Remove dentures. Minimize swallowing during neck acquisition
notes.additional_recons: MIP and 3D VR reconstructions of vessels. Curved MPR of carotids

safety.allergy: Check allergy history and renal function

notes.tech: Aortic arch to skull base. Bolus tracking in arch. Submillimeter. Minimize swallowing during scan
notes.nursing: 20G IV antecubital preferred
notes.rad: Assess carotid bifurcations. Stenosis grading. Vertebral arteries. Dissection. Plaque morphology
notes.tips: Minimize swallowing. Submillimeter acquisition
notes.additional_recons: Curved MPR both carotid bifurcations. Measure stenosis (NASCET). 3D VR. MIP

notes.tech: NC Head then delayed venous CTV (60-90 sec). Skull base to vertex. Assess venous sinuses
notes.rad: NC: hemorrhage. CTV: filling defects in sinuses. Venous thrombosis. Cortical vein thrombosis
notes.tips: Delayed timing 60-90 sec. Look for filling defects
notes.additional_recons: 3D VR venogram. MIP maximum intensity projection. Document filling defects

notes.tech: Minimize patient motion. Gantry angle parallel to skull base to reduce orbital dose. Ensure head straight
notes.nursing: No IV required. Explain importance of staying still
notes.rad: Look for hyperdense MCA sign. Assess grey-white differentiation. Check for hemorrhage and mass effect
notes.tips: Remove dentures and hearing aids. Secure head in holder
notes.additional_recons: Thin slice 1.25mm if subtle fracture suspected

title: Pregnant Trauma CT AP
author: Dr. Anderson
position: Supine with left lateral tilt if possible

notes.tech: Portal venous phase 70s. SINGLE PHASE to minimize fetal radiation. Shield uterus if injury distant. Document weeks gestation
notes.nursing: Pregnancy documented. Fetal heart tones if equipment available. Shield if possible
notes.rad: Assess maternal injuries. Minimize fetal radiation exposure. Document placental injury if visible
notes.tips: Document gestational age. Shield fetus if possible. Minimize radiation

title: Trauma CTA Chest with PV CT AP
author: Dr. Lee

contrast.timing: Dual phase: CTA Chest arterial + Portal venous AP

notes.tech: TWO acquisitions: 1) CTA CHEST arterial (bolus track) 2) Portal venous ABDOMEN/PELVIS 70s. Chest arterial for aorta/vessels
notes.nursing: Large bore IV 18-20G. Verify flow
notes.rad: Chest arterial: aortic injury (intimal flap pseudoaneurysm). AP portal venous: solid organ injury
notes.tips: Trauma indication. Fast scan. Good IV essential
notes.additional_recons: 3D aorta and great vessels. Curved MPR aorta. Grade aortic injury

title: Trauma Chest CT
author: Dr. Martinez
position: Supine with arms raised if possible

notes.tech: Single acquisition lung apices to costophrenic angles. RIB REFORMATS required. Submillimeter acquisition
notes.nursing: Trauma precautions. Arms up if able
notes.rad: Pneumothorax hemothorax. Rib fractures (count and location). Pulmonary contusion. Aortic injury. Sternal/scapular fractures
notes.tips: Submillimeter acquisition critical for rib detail
notes.additional_recons: Dedicated rib reformats (oblique sagittal each rib). Count fractures. 3D chest wall

contrast.timing: Triple phase: NC + Arterial + Portal venous

notes.tech: RAPID triple phase: 1) NC CAP (hematoma) 2) Arterial CAP (active bleed bolus track 25-30s) 3) Portal venous CAP (70s). STAT protocol
notes.nursing: Large bore IV 18G minimum. Blood products ready
notes.rad: NC: retroperitoneal hematoma. Arterial: active extravasation aneurysm morphology. Portal: solid organs
notes.tips: STAT protocol. Minimize delays. Notify vascular surgery
notes.additional_recons: Measure aneurysm. Identify bleeding site. EVAR measurements if stable

title: Trauma Head C-Spine and Facial Bones
author: Dr. Johnson

notes.tech: THREE acquisitions: 1) Head 2) C-spine 3) Facial bones. Face: submillimeter helical for 3D. C-collar remains
notes.nursing: C-collar precautions. Document mechanism of injury
notes.rad: Head: intracranial injury. C-spine: fractures. Face: Le Fort midface orbital mandible fractures
notes.tips: C-collar on. Remove dentures if safe
notes.additional_recons: 3D face reconstruction. Le Fort classification. Orbital floor assessment

title: Trauma Head and C-Spine
author: Dr. Smith
position: Supine head-first. Cervical collar in place

notes.tech: TWO acquisitions: 1) Head vertex to C1 2) C-spine skull base to T1. Head: 5mm axial. C-spine: 0.625mm with reformats. Minimize movement
notes.nursing: Maintain cervical precautions. C-collar remains on. Document GCS
notes.rad: Head: acute hemorrhage skull fractures. C-spine: fractures alignment ligamentous injury
notes.tips: Keep C-collar on. Minimize patient movement
notes.additional_recons: C-spine: Sagittal and coronal bone reformats. 3D if complex fracture

contrast.roi: Abdominal aorta or proximal to injury

notes.tech: Extend coverage based on injury. Aorta to ankles if bilateral. May do unilateral focused study. Arterial phase
notes.nursing: 18-20G IV. May need proximal IV if arm injury
notes.rad: Assess arterial injury: transection pseudoaneurysm occlusion extravasation. Evaluate fracture relationship to vessels
notes.tips: Tailor coverage to injury. Fast acquisition
notes.additional_recons: MIP and 3D VR. Document vascular injury. Measure vessel caliber

title: CTA Abdomen Pelvis
author: Dr. Martinez
premedication: Oral contrast optional - omit for vascular indication

notes.tech: Caudocranial scan direction. Include renal arteries to femoral bifurcation minimum
notes.nursing: 18-20G IV antecubital
notes.rad: Measure AAA if present. Assess renal and mesenteric arteries. Evaluate iliac vessels
notes.tips: Arms raised. No oral contrast for pure vascular study
notes.additional_recons: 3D VR and curved MPR. Measure AAA in 3 planes

title: CTA Chest
author: Dr. Johnson
clinical_indications: Thoracic aortic aneurysm (not involving the aortic root)

notes.tech: Choose ROI based on indication - ascending aorta for aortic pathology or main PA for PE
notes.nursing: 20G IV minimum
notes.rad: Assess aorta and great vessels. Measure aneurysm if present. Look for dissection flap
notes.tips: Arms fully raised
notes.additional_recons: 3D VR of thoracic vasculature

title: CTA Chest Abdomen Pelvis
author: Dr. Smith
position: Supine with arms raised above head

recons.notes: Sagittal MIP and curved MPR of aorta

notes.tech: Single acquisition from thoracic inlet to pubic symphysis. Caudocranial direction. Bolus track in descending aorta
notes.nursing: 20G IV minimum. Antecubital or proximal forearm preferred
notes.rad: Assess entire aorta for dissection/aneurysm. Measure aortic dimensions. Check branch vessels
notes.tips: Arms completely raised. ECG monitoring if known dissection
notes.additional_recons: 3D VR and curved MPR of entire aorta

title: CTA DIEP Flap Pre-operative
author: Dr. Williams
clinical_indications: Pre-operative planning for DIEP flap breast reconstruction
position: Supine with arms at sides or on chest

notes.tech: Scan from mid-liver to greater trochanters. Remove tight-fitting underwear. If patient can exercise, do leg lifts on table before injection.
notes.rad: Map perforator locations. Measure vessel caliber. Identify dominant perforators. Note relationship to umbilicus. Prefer perforators below umbilicus.
notes.tips: Arms positioned to not obscure anterior abdominal wall
notes.additional_recons: 3D VR color-coded perforator map. Measure distances from umbilicus

title: CTA Lower Extremity Free Flap
author: Dr. Kim
clinical_indications: Pre-operative planning for free flap harvest (fibula ALT anterolateral thigh)

notes.tech: Scan from iliac crest to ankle. Focus on perforators in region of interest. Arterial phase critical for mapping
notes.rad: Map perforator vessels. Measure vessel caliber and length. Identify dominant pedicle. Note anatomic variants
notes.tips: Legs straight and not rotated. Mark skin over region of interest if possible
notes.additional_recons: Curved MPR of main vessels. Measure perforator locations from bony landmarks

title: CTA Lower Extremity Runoff for PAD
author: Dr. Anderson
position: Supine with arms raised. Legs straight

series.name: CTA Arterial
series.notes: May need slower table speed if severe PAD

series.name: CTA Runoff
series.notes: Runoff phase to evaluate distal vessels

notes.tech: Scan from diaphragm to toes. Tape feet together. Use automatic bolus tracking. Extend delay if known severe PAD. Cover tibial vessels to ankle
notes.nursing: 18-20G IV antecubital, flow rate up to 6 mL/s
notes.rad: Assess aortoiliac femoral popliteal and tibial vessels. Grade stenoses. Identify occlusions. Assess runoff vessels
notes.tips: Ensure legs are straight and not rotated. Remove shoes and metal
notes.additional_recons: MIP and 3D VR. Curved MPR of each arterial segment. Bone subtraction for vessels.

notes.tech: Arterial phase at 25 sec for vessel assessment. Portal venous at 70 sec for bowel perfusion. High flow rate critical
notes.nursing: 18-20G IV required for 5 mL/s flow. Must be patent
notes.rad: Arterial: assess celiac SMA IMA origins. Portal: look for bowel wall enhancement. Check for pneumatosis
notes.tips: Fast scan. High flow rate essential
notes.additional_recons: MIP and 3D VR of celiac and SMA. Curved MPR of vessels

title: CTA Pelvis Cyclist Iliac Artery Maneuver
author: Dr. Rodriguez
position: Supine initially then with hip flexion

contrast.volume: Split bolus: 1st injection 1.1 mL/kg + 2nd injection 1.1 mL/kg
contrast.timing: Dual position: Resting + Hip flexion cycling position

notes.tech: TWO acquisitions: 1) Resting supine 2) Hip flexion simulating cycling position. Bilateral imaging for comparison
notes.rad: Compare resting vs flexed position. Look for iliac artery kinking stenosis or occlusion with hip flexion. Common in competitive cyclists
notes.tips: Position patient with knees bent and hips flexed to simulate cycling. May need positioning aids
notes.additional_recons: Side-by-side MIP of rest vs flexion. Measure degree of stenosis. 3D VR

safety.allergy: Check allergy history. Explain hip flexion positioning

title: CTA Pelvis Prostate Artery Embolization
author: Dr. Jackson
clinical_indications: Pre-procedural planning for prostate artery embolization

notes.tech: Scan from L3 to proximal femur. Arterial phase essential. Focus on internal iliac branches and prostate supply
notes.nursing: 18-20G IV | Chcek BP for nitroglycerin administration, check for contraindications
notes.rad: Identify prostate artery origins (usually anterior division of internal iliac). Map anatomy for IR. Note variants and anastomoses
notes.tips: Full bladder helpful for prostate visualization. Coordinate with IR before scan
notes.additional_recons: 3D VR with prostate vessels highlighted. Curved MPR of internal iliac branches. Measure vessel diameters

title: CTA Popliteal Entrapment
author: Dr. Thompson
position: Supine with legs extended in neutral position

series.name: CTA Plantarflexion
series.notes: Patient actively plantarflexes both feet - point toes

notes.tech: TWO acquisitions required: 1) Neutral position 2) Active plantarflexion. Both legs scanned for comparison. Coach patient on plantarflexion technique
notes.nursing: 18-20G IV antecubital
notes.rad: Compare neutral vs plantarflexion images. Look for popliteal artery compression deviation or occlusion with plantarflexion. Assess muscle anatomy
notes.tips: Coach patient on maintaining plantarflexion during second acquisition. Use foot straps if needed
notes.additional_recons: Side-by-side comparison of neutral vs plantarflexion. 3D VR showing muscle-vessel relationship

safety.allergy: Check allergy history. Explain plantarflexion maneuver to patient

title: CTA SCAD/FMD Protocol
author: Dr. Hayes
position: Supine with arms initially UP then DOWN

contrast.timing: Multi-phase: NC Head + CTA Neck + CTA CAP arms up + Post-contrast Head arms down

notes.tech: FOUR acquisitions: 1) NC Head arms down 2) CTA Neck bolus track 3) CTA CAP arms up 4) Post Head arms down. Patient repositions arms between scans
notes.nursing: 20G IV minimum. Verify good flow for multiple phases
notes.rad: Screen all vascular beds for FMD. Look for beading stenosis aneurysm dissection. Assess renal carotid vertebral intracranial arteries
notes.tips: Coach patient on arm repositioning. Multiple phases require good IV. Plan scan sequence carefully
notes.additional_recons: Comprehensive MIP and 3D VR of all vascular beds. Measure vessel diameters. Document FMD findings

safety.allergy: Check allergy history. Explain arm repositioning

title: CTA Upper Extremity
author: Dr. Davis
position: Supine with affected arm raised above head or at side depending on indication

notes.tech: Scan from aortic arch to fingertips. May need bilateral for comparison. Position arm to demonstrate pathology | Inject into contralateral arm
notes.nursing: 20G IV in contralateral arm
notes.rad: Assess subclavian axillary brachial radial ulnar arteries. Look for stenosis occlusion or injury
notes.tips: Position arm to avoid overlap with torso. May need special positioning for TOS
notes.additional_recons: MIP and 3D VR. Subtract bones for vessel visualization

safety.allergy: Check allergy history. IV in opposite arm

contrast.timing: Triple phase: Arterial + Portal Venous + Delayed

series.name: Delayed Phase
series.notes: Extended delay to see pooling of contrast

recons.notes: Look for contrast pooling in bowel

notes.tech: High flow rate critical for arterial phase. Scan arterial at 25 sec then portal at 70 sec then delayed at 90-180 sec. Look for active extravasation
notes.nursing: Large bore IV 18-20G essential. Verify with saline test
notes.rad: Look for arterial extravasation (early) and pooling (delayed). Note location and potential source vessel
notes.tips: Arms raised to avoid artifacts. Fast table speed to cover area quickly in arterial phase
notes.additional_recons: MIP of all three phases side-by-side for comparison

safety.renal: eGFR > 30 preferred but can proceed emergently
safety.allergy: Document allergy history. Emergency indication overrides mild allergy

notes.tech: Scan at 180 seconds for venous phase. Slower injection rate OK for venous imaging. Scan from diaphragm to femoral veins
notes.rad: Assess IVC iliac femoral veins for thrombosis. Look for compression (May-Thurner). Measure vessel caliber for filter sizing
notes.tips: Arms raised. May add leg veins if DVT suspected
notes.additional_recons: MIP venograms. 3D VR of venous system

notes.tech: Scan at 180 seconds. Include SVC through femoral veins. May need arm injection for SVC assessment
notes.nursing: 18-20G IV - may need bilateral arm IVs for SVC
notes.rad: Assess SVC IVC and major tributaries. Look for thrombosis compression or tumor invasion
notes.tips: Arms raised. For SVC consider bilateral arm injection
notes.additional_recons: 3D venogram MIP. Curved MPR of SVC and IVC

safety.allergy: Check allergy history. May need bilateral IVs
